plan.estimand: Main effect of 2-level factor in 3×2 factorial ANOVA
plan.hypothesis: H₀: factor B main effect = 0; H₁: factor B main effect ≠ 0
assumptions: Balanced design with equal cell sizes
Independent observations within and across cells
Normal distributions in each cell
Homogeneity of variance across all 6 cells
All 6 cell means are freely estimated
F-test for main effect of 2-level factor (factor B)
Numerator df = 1 corresponding to factor B
clarification_questions: Design confirmation: 3×2 factorial with factor A (3 levels) and factor B (2 levels) yields 6 cells. Testing the factor B main effect with 1 numerator df via F-test. Denominator df = 6(n − 1). Is this the correct model structure and hypothesis?
scientific_notes: Partial eta-squared η²_p = 0.06 is the effect size for the factor B main effect in the context of this factorial design.
Conversion from η²_p to noncentrality λ requires denominator df, which depends on the sample size per cell (n): df_denom = 6(n − 1).
This is an iterative inversion problem: we search for the minimum integer n per cell such that power at (1, 6(n−1)) with λ derived from η²_p ≥ 0.80.
The relationship: η²_p = λ / (λ + df_denom); solving for λ: λ = η²_p × df_denom / (1 − η²_p).
